summary: Argentic introduces the internet's first machine-native toll booth, enabling AI agents to pay in Bitcoin Lightning for web access. This system eliminates accounts and API keys, offering cheap and fast machine-to-machine payments.

headline_marked: [[US intervention killed Japan's ambitious TRON OS]] for desktops, while embedded version thrived
headline: US intervention killed Japan's ambitious TRON OS for desktops, while embedded version thrived
summary: Japan's TRON Project aimed to create a vertically integrated OS with a hypermedia document model and custom CPU. Its desktop variant, BTRON, was effectively halted after a 1989 US trade report.
details: In 1984, Japan launched the TRON Project, an ambitious OS initiative aiming to replace file systems with hypermedia and run on custom CPUs. Its desktop version, BTRON, was targeted by a 1989 US trade report as an unfair barrier, effectively ending its widespread adoption. Meanwhile, its embedded counterpart, ITRON, became one of history's most deployed OS.

Led by Ken Sakamura at the University of Tokyo, TRON sought to build Japan's entire digital infrastructure, from microcontrollers to workstations. It comprised five sub-architectures, including ITRON for embedded systems and BTRON for personal computers.

The project developed its own TRON VLSI CPU, manufactured by Hitachi, and a unique TRON keyboard layout for efficient Japanese input. It also proposed a real-time peripheral bus, micro-BTRON, though it never shipped commercially. The aim was a fully integrated platform without existing compatibility debt.

TRON Code, its character encoding system, was highly advanced, supporting 1.5 million characters across 31 planes. By 1999, it covered 130,000 characters, including extensive CJK sets and Braille as a first-class plane, exceeding Unicode's CJK coverage for over a decade.

The TRON Association, established in 1986, included major Japanese electronics companies like Hitachi, Mitsubishi, Fujitsu, and NEC. Foreign companies could also join, and the specifications were royalty-free.
caption:
